title: Llama flow, dense Llama and Mistral, and Mixtral MoE under the same family string (split by expert_count)

installs.name: mistral-7b-q4_k_m
installs.note: the dense half's head_dim-128 install: the one shape where the decode_attention sweep can engage the GQA-shared kernel

installs.name: tinyllama
installs.note: head_dim 64 with 32 q over 4 kv heads: the GQA-shared decode kernel does not serve this shape and the dispatcher falls back to barrier (measured 2026-10-29)

recommended.why: the dense half runs the single-command-buffer chunked driver with batched attention (the 2026-10-02 release artifacts); the walk is the fallback, not the default
Mixtral's routed half is Step 1 with RoutedSlot; the batched arm is opt-in and unmeasured on this flow

default on (llama-flow flip, 2026-10-29): the GQA-shared decode kernel read +5.73% on mistral7b; TURBOSPARK_ATTN_DECODE_KERNEL=barrier restores it and is the sweep's kill arm; head_dim-64 installs fall back to barrier in the encoder regardless

sweeps.description: the batched prefill arm against the per-token loop on the dense half
the barrier kernel opt-out against the default GQA-shared decode kernel

open_questions: a Steel arm for the dense half (the batched attention kernel is in; the GEMM is scalar)

the llama-flow decode default flipped to gqa on 2026-10-29 for dense installs on timing wins and greedy identity; a dense_kl gate on mistral7b is still owed, and Mixtral (same family string) keeps barrier until it has its own verdict
Mixtral: the routed batch arm and the slot count
traps: dense Llama and Mixtral share this family string: kl_class_for decides the gate class by expert_count, and the dispatch probe and stand-ins apply to the dense half only
BF16 matrices (MiniCPM-style trunks) refuse the batched arm
head_dim-64 GGUF installs (tinyllama) silently fall back to the barrier kernel when TURBOSPARK_ATTN_DECODE_KERNEL=gqa: the engagement guard rejects every such run, so the arm is never a measurement
